- When sentiment turns negative (or shows strong bearish signals) in the recent history, reduce forecasted price targets, especially in the short-to-medium horizon (next 5–15 days).  
- If model forecasts show a sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% above recent mean) followed by a true outcome that reverses or underperforms, apply a downward correction of 5–15% in the following 5–10 days.  
- In periods with high sentiment volatility (e.g., alternating +1 and -1), model forecasts tend to overreact — dampen the forecast slope and avoid sharp directional moves.  
- If the model consistently overestimates prices in the 30-day horizon (especially after a recent spike), apply a 3–7% downward bias to the final 5–10 days of the forecast.  
- When sentiment is uniformly positive over 5+ days, model may overfit upward momentum — cap the forecast at 1.5x the 14-day moving average to avoid over-optimism.  
- If the true outcome is consistently below the model’s 30-day forecast, especially after a recent dip, consider a mean-reversion adjustment: shift forecast downward by 2–5% for the next 7–14 days.
